sections.title: The Roman Watermill Complex at Barbegal
sections.passageMd:
The Barbegal aqueduct and mill complex is a Roman watermill installation located in southern France. Described as the greatest known concentration of mechanical power in the ancient world, the complex comprised sixteen overshot water wheels arranged in two parallel sets of eight down a steep hillside. Hydraulic engineers estimate that the facility could grind up to twenty-five tonnes of grain daily, enough to produce flour for the entire population of the nearby city of Arelate (modern Arles), which numbered approximately twelve thousand inhabitants in the second century AD.

Excavations led by archaeologist Fernand Benoit in the late 1930s revealed that each mill race was driven by a single stone aqueduct that divided into two channels at the crest of the hill. Carbonate encrustations preserved on the surviving stonework indicate that the waterwheels operated almost continuously throughout the year, rather than intermittently or seasonally. A notable feature of the Barbegal mills was the use of wood for both the gears and axle shafts, while the flumes and retaining structures were constructed from dressed limestone blocks and hydraulic mortar.

Recent isotopic analysis of the millstones has demonstrated that the basalt utilised in their manufacture originated from quarries in the Massif Central, nearly two hundred kilometres north of the site. This finding disproved earlier theories asserting that local limestone was used for the grindstones. Transporting such dense volcanic stone over that distance required substantial logistical organisation, suggesting that the Roman imperial state played a direct role in funding and managing the complex. Furthermore, researchers found no evidence of slave quarters near the mills, leading social historians to conclude that the workforce was composed of free paid labourers who resided in adjacent farming settlements.

questionGroups.instructionMd: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1? In boxes 1–5 on your answer sheet, write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, or NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

questions.promptMd: The Barbegal complex contained sixteen water wheels arranged in four equal rows.
questions.explanationMd: The complex comprised sixteen overshot water wheels arranged in two parallel sets of eight, not four rows.

questions.promptMd: The flour produced at Barbegal was sufficient to feed the entire population of Arelate.
questions.explanationMd: Hydraulic engineers estimate the facility could grind enough to produce flour for the entire population of the nearby city of Arelate.

questions.promptMd: The waterwheels at Barbegal operated only during the autumn harvest season.
questions.explanationMd: Carbonate encrustations indicate that the waterwheels operated almost continuously throughout the year, rather than intermittently or seasonally.

questions.promptMd: The millstones at Barbegal were manufactured from local limestone.
questions.explanationMd: Isotopic analysis disproved earlier theories asserting that local limestone was used for the grindstones, showing basalt was used instead.

questions.promptMd: The Roman imperial state levied a special tax on grain ground at Barbegal.
questions.explanationMd: The passage mentions state management and funding, but there is no mention of a tax levied on grain.
